speaker: Marla
line: Welcome to Saltmarsh, traveller. The tide is out and the boats are waiting.
The harbourmaster is counting crates again. Pay her no mind.
SALTMARSH — DEEP WATER BERTH 4

speaker: Corvin
line: You'll want the long rope. Short ones fray on the pilings.
Rope (long) — thirty fathoms of good hemp.

speaker: Marla
line:
Mind the gap between the second and third step.
Nobody built these docks for tall feet.
Watchtower Notice: no lamps after the third bell.

speaker: Corvin
line: Hear that? The bell is ringing early.
A gull lands on a crate and refuses to leave.

speaker: Marla
line: The old wreck came in with the storm. Folk say it still has cargo aboard.
Wreck of the Galloway — entered at your own risk

speaker: Corvin
line: I'll hold the lantern. You go first, you're the one with the sword.
Rusted Cutlass. Notched, but balanced.
Water sloshes somewhere below the deck plates.

speaker: Marla
line: Nobody said a word about the smell. Nobody ever does.

speaker: Corvin
line: Two candles down and something is still burning back there.
Cargo Manifest (water damaged) — only the last line is legible: 'six crates, sealed'
Sealed Crate. The locks are new for an old ship.

speaker: Marla
line: Set it down. Whatever is in there, the harbourmaster can open it.

speaker: Corvin
line: That's not a lock. That's a warning.
Below Decks — no lanterns and no running
A boy in an oilskin coat watches from the far rung of the ladder.

speaker: Boy
line: You opened it.

speaker: Marla
line: We opened nothing. The sea opened it.

speaker: Boy
line: Then the sea will want it back. My grandmother says deep water always collects.
Salt-Crusted Key. It fits nothing on this ship.

speaker: Corvin
line: Tide's turning. Ladder. Now.
Harbour Gate — closed between the second and third bell

speaker: Têvance
line: You're late, and you're wet, and the crate is already gone. Come inside anyway.

speaker: Têvance
line: Tea first. Questions cost extra after the second cup.
Maps of the Outer Banks, folded, and one of them is wet.

speaker: Boy
line: The harbourmaster counted the crates twice. She always counts them twice.

speaker: Têvance
line: She counts them because one is never where she left it. Don't tell her I said so.
The bell rings twice, then stops, as if someone remembered it was ringing.

speaker: Têvance
line: Take the long map. The short one only shows where the safe water used to be.
TOWN LEDGER — balance owed to the harbourmaster: see the last page

speaker: Boy
line: He's asking about the sealed crate. Everyone who asks about it leaves town.

speaker: Chef Ondine
line: Two fish. One burnt on purpose and one by accident.
Smoked Eel — six coppers, or a favour you can name later

speaker: Chef Ondine
line: The wreck folk pay in buttons now. Buttons don't cook.
